newsitem.title: BELGIUM: South Africa presses EU for better farm trade deal.
newsitem.headline: South Africa presses EU for better farm trade deal.

text.p: South Africa pressed on Friday for better terms for its agricultural exports in a proposed free trade agreement with the European Union, EU officials said.

The officials said that in a meeting, EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler told South African Farm Minister Derek Hannekom that Brussels had to respect a mandate given by EU member states as well as preferences granted African, Caribbean and Pacific (ACP) countries under the Lome convention.
South Africa says that a proposed free trade agreement with the EU would exclude 39 percent of its farm exports.
In reply to complaints that subsidised EU beef exports were undermining the South African market, Fischler said that export refunds had been cut by 35 percent since the start of 1997.
The complaints follow a surge in EU beef exports to 41,000 tonnes in 1995, from 3,500 tonnes in 1992.
The EU was waiting for more data from South Africa to prove that its livestock producers had suffered losses, EU officials said.
Problems concerning South African exports of ostrich meat and wine were also raised.
South African officials could not immediately be reached for comment.
The next EU-South African ministerial review of the negotiations is due to take place in July.
